# Tracetoon

**PRs with receipts. And comics.**

Your coding agent already kept the receipts: what you asked for, what it
changed, what actually ran. Tracetoon turns them into a pull request reviewers
can trust. It works with Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Factory Droid, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo CLI, Kiro, Cline, Junie, Devin, Goose, Qwen Code and Crush.

```sh
npx tracetoon@latest setup
```

That installs the Tracetoon skill into every agent it finds and adds a hook, so
the next time you ask your agent to open a PR, Tracetoon writes it. Restart the
agent afterwards.

## Why use it

- **Written from what happened.** Your agent already logged what you asked for, what it changed and which commands ran; Tracetoon writes the description from that record, so it can say why the change was made and what was tested, not just what the diff shows.
- **Every claim checked.** Each factual sentence has to trace back to the session evidence, independent reviewers check the draft, and the Validation section comes from recorded test and build runs instead of being typed by the model.
- **Cheaper to write.** A compact, cited evidence brief built in an embedded graph database lets the agent draft without rereading raw logs.
- **Safe to post.** Private paths and secrets are redacted from the evidence, and a leak scan runs before anything is posted.
- **Follows the house rules.** It reads the repository's PR template, contribution guide and AI-disclosure policy and writes to them.
- **Works with your agents.** Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Factory Droid, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Kilo CLI, Kiro, Cline, Junie, Devin, Goose, Qwen Code and Crush, as an agent skill, a CLI or an MCP server.
- **A comic on top.** An optional one-off comic about the change, which reviewers actually read.

## Results

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **72–9** | both judges preferred the Tracetoon PR over Claude Code (Opus 5.5) writing alone |
| **111–19** | the same on Codex (Sol 6.1) |
| **−50%** | factual errors per PR on Opus 5.5 (0.16 vs 0.32) |
| **−28% / −73%** | cost per PR on Claude Code / Codex in a 500k-token session |

prbench: 61 real PRs from 12 repositories, each written 3 times by the agent alone and by the same agent in the same session with Tracetoon, 2 AI judges per provider in both orders; a pick counts only when both agree. Cost assumes a session carrying 500k tokens with subscription caching. Full results, methods and caveats: https://tracetoon.ai/vs-native.html

## Install for good

For a lasting `tracetoon` command (and a PR hook that outlives the npx cache):
`npm install -g tracetoon`, then `tracetoon setup`. Other routes (the curl
and PowerShell installers, plugin marketplaces):
https://github.com/Tracetoon/tracetoon#-quick-start

Needs `git` and the GitHub CLI (`gh`), signed in. Prebuilt binaries: Linux and
macOS (x64, arm64), Windows x64. The binary comes from an optional dependency
(`@tracetoon/cli-<platform>-<arch>`), so don't install with `--omit=optional`.

## For agents

```sh
npx tracetoon@latest setup --json     # install the skill into every agent found, add the PR hook
npx tracetoon@latest doctor --json    # check git, gh and the install
```

Every command accepts `--json`; `tracetoon commands --json` lists them all.
`tracetoon mcp` serves the same flow over MCP on stdio.

- How agents use Tracetoon: https://github.com/Tracetoon/tracetoon/blob/main/AGENTS.md
- Install routes for each agent host: https://github.com/Tracetoon/tracetoon/blob/main/docs/agents/install.md
